children: plans to invest $100 million in Colombia in 2027 to advance exploration and permitting at its flagship project in the central department of Caldas, a company executive said on Tuesday, in a boost to the government's drive to attract foreign investment into the mining sector.
Colombian Vice President Jose Manuel Restrepo said on X that Collective could invest as much as $1 billion more through 2030 if it secures the required license for the project.
Ari Sussman, Collective's chairman, said the 2027 spending would fund continued exploration and help move the project through licensing
The company's most advanced asset is the Apollo deposit within its 100%-owned Guayabales project, located near the Marmato mining district in Caldas

Collective said in September that Apollo hosts an initial indicated resource of 2.58 million gold-equivalent ounces and an inferred resource of 2.83 million gold-equivalent ounces, and that it was targeting submission of an environmental license application in the second half of 2027
The company has said early works and construction could begin in the second half of 2029, subject to studies, financing and permits
The investment comes as President Abelardo De La Espriella's government seeks to revive mining and energy investment after taking office in August

Colombia has been trying to position itself as a supplier of critical minerals and has stepped up international outreach in the sector, including signing cooperation arrangements with the United States in September
